diagnostics.message: `:resource.aws_ecs_cluster_capacity_providers.this` builds its `capacity_providers`/`default_capacity_provider_strategy` lists from `var.autoscaling_capacity_providers` names, so it has no data reference to `:resource.aws_ecs_capacity_provider.this`; the existing `depends_on` only orders the initial create/destroy of the whole set. Per the AWS provider docs for both `aws_ecs_capacity_provider` and `aws_ecs_cluster_capacity_providers`, AWS will not delete a capacity provider that is still associated with a cluster, so when a capacity provider is forced to be replaced (e.g. name or ASG change) the association must be recreated before the old provider is deleted — an operational ordering neither an attribute reference nor the current depends_on expresses. Wire the association to the created provider resources (or add `lifecycle { replace_triggered_by = [aws_ecs_capacity_provider.this] }`) so the old provider is detached first.

fix.expression: distinct(concat([for k, v in var.default_capacity_provider_strategy : try(coalesce(v.name, k))], aws_ecs_capacity_provider.this != null ? [for k, v in aws_ecs_capacity_provider.this : v.name] : []))
